answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. This design turns the attacker's greatest weapon — scale — into its weakest point, because scale is exactly what becomes unaffordable to maintain. Consider a tide as the anchor of the cost.
